editorial:
Imagine growing up in the wild of Kenya, where your best friend isn't a kid from school, but a massive adult lion. That is exactly the life young Tina has. Her stepfather thinks it is a dream way to grow up, but her mother is totally freaked out. She worries that Tina is becoming too wild and losing her touch with the real world. The vibe is a mix of a beautiful nature trip and a tense family fight. You get to see the gorgeous African landscape while watching a mother try to save her daughter from a life of danger.

What really works here is the tension between the parents. The acting is solid, and seeing a child bond with a predator keeps you on edge. The pacing is a bit slow in the middle, but the drama makes up for it. If you love stories about nature and family secrets, you will dig this. It is a great pick for a quiet weekend night.
endingExplained: Everything comes to a head when the biological father arrives to take Tina back to the US. The tension peaks during a final confrontation between the humans and the lion. It turns out the mother's motives were more complex than just saving Tina. In the end, the wild nature of the lion and the girl's bond prove too strong to break. Tina stays behind, choosing her wild life over a boring city existence in Connecticut.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves animal stories and family conflict.
